plugin.name: Annotation Processing Tool
plugin.description: Provides support for annotation processing integrated into the IDE, as opposed to running as a part of the compilation process. The plugin supports configuration of individual project modules and JARs with annotation processors. Annotation processing kicks in whenever a file's content changes, either due to being saved in the IDE or as a result of external changes; renaming, moving, and deletion of a file also invokes annotation processing. Those who are familiar with annotation processing in the Eclipse IDE will find this plugin's mechanics very similar.
plugin.change-notes:
• #22

    In multi-module Maven projects, annotation processors may see outdated class files instead of the latest source code, especially when automatic recompilation is disabled. The plugin now automatically adds dependent modules to the source path during processing, ensuring annotation processors use the same up-to-date sources that developers see.

  • #24

    Annotation processing previously handled affected sources only within a single module, ignoring cross-module dependencies. The plugin now detects when changes in one module affect sources in dependent modules and automatically reprocesses affected files in those modules to ensure that results are consistent.

plugin.name: APT Synchroniser
plugin.description: Provides support for plugins dependent on the APT plugin in the form of synchronisation facilities.

plugin.name: Trident Genesis (TG) Tools
plugin.description: This plugin facilitates the development of TG applications.
plugin.change-notes:
The plugin has been enhanced to assist with adopting save-with-fetch throughout TG-based applications. Please refer to the TG issue #2612 for more information.

  1. Several inspections have been added, all of which have prefix "TG". They can be found among all inspections in IDE settings (Editor > Inspections). Some inspections are actionable — they suggest a quick fix to automatically adjust the code.

    Although inspections always run in the background while editing a file, they can also be launched manually for more than one file at a time. This can be done by invoking action "Run Inspection by Name" (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+i).

  2. Several intention actions have been added, which become available in certain contexts. Press Alt+Enter when editing a file to display available intentions. Intentions provided by this plugin can be found among all intentions in IDE settings (Editor > Intentions) in section "TG".
